summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs for Atlas Health. Demo focused on correlating request IDs across traces, diagnosing high-latency tail requests, KV cache effects, and configuring alerting/retention. Customers asked about data residency, KMS/HSM support, SSO, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: share security docs, run a short benchmark, and provision a trial account.
topics: Error analysis and stack traces mapping
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-30 15:00 UTC; Duration approx 46 minutes; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Atlas Platform), Ethan Morales (Atlas ML Infra), Laura Kim (Atlas Security)

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a 30-ish minute walkthrough of the Console tracing and request logs, then leave time for Q&A. Can you all hear me OK?
00:12 Priya (Atlas): Yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya. We're mainly focused on how to debug production errors and understand latency spikes.
00:20 Maya: Great, that's exactly what Connor will demo. Quick context - Atlas is evaluating hosted vs dedicated capacity, and wants visibility into per-request traces, is that right?
00:30 Ethan: Yeah and also how the KV cache affects tail latency for our long-chat product, sometimes tokens blow out.
00:36 Connor (Redwood SE): Awesome, jumping in. First screen is the Traces view in the Console. You can see request-level timelines, spans for routing, model inference, tokenization, and any downstream calls. I'm going to pull up an example trace with a big latency tail.
00:52 (screen share)
01:05 Connor: Here we have a 1.2s request, broken out - tokenization 30ms, model inference 980ms, network 110ms. You can correlate that to a request id and drill into the model variant used, the quantization profile, and whether it hit prefix cache.
01:26 Priya: When you say "prefix cache" is that the KV cache?
01:30 Connor: Yes, sorry internal shorthand. Sometimes the transcript will show "K V cash" or similar, transcription aside. The KV cache is shown as a span; if it misses you see a longer model inference span.
01:42 Ethan: Can we filter traces by route or by user id? We need to see per-tenant behavior.
01:50 Connor: Yes - filters on the top let you scope by route, model, customer id, or custom tags. We recommend tagging upstream requests with your tenant id so traces correlate end-to-end.
02:05 Laura (Security): Quick security question - where are these logs stored and how long do they persist? We need 12 months for audit purposes.
02:12 Maya: Good question. By default hosted retains 90 days, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and export to S3 or your GCS bucket. We also support sending audit logs to your SIEM and KMS for key management.
02:28 Laura: Do you support HSM-backed keys?
02:32 Maya: Yes, HSM via customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated. We'll include the exact KMS/HSM note in the security pack.
02:40 (Connor navigates)
02:52 Connor: Next is Error Analysis. The Console aggregates error types, shows stack-like messages returned from models or runtime, and provides sample request payloads. You can click a failure to replay a request in a safe sandbox.
03:10 Priya: Replay - is that actual data replayed to model endpoints? We have PHI in some prompts.
03:18 Connor: The replay in the Console redacts PII by default and runs in an isolated sandbox; for PHI/PII workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or Private and also will support configurable redaction rules. We'll note that in the security doc.
03:35 Ethan: How do you map model errors to code traces? We have an in-house transform before calling the API, want to see where errors originate.
03:45 Connor: We let you attach instrumentation and custom spans. If you wrap the call with our SDK instrumentation or add the request id as a header, the Console will stitch the upstream span to the inference span. That stitching is what lets you see whether the transform or the model invocation caused the error.
04:05 (short pause)
04:18 Priya: Can we set alerts on error rates per route?
04:22 Connor: Yep, alerting ties into the metrics - error rate, p95/p99 latency, token consumption. Alerts can be routed to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook.
04:30 Priya: Good. Also curious about canary rollouts - if we push a quantized variant how do we see regressions?
04:40 Connor: Console supports rollouts with comparison dashboards. You can do A/B or canary and Console will compute quality deltas on your eval set or on production golden prompts, and it surface regressions in error analysis.
04:55 Ethan: That eval set, is it uploaded to Redwood? Any concerns on sensitive prompts?
05:02 Maya: You can upload eval sets into your private workspace; for stricter controls use a Private deployment so data never leaves your VPC. We'll also include guidance on encryption in transit and at rest.
05:18 (screen change to Request Logs view)
05:25 Connor: Request logs are more raw - each line includes a request id, timestamp, route, model variant, latency, token counts, and a pointer to the trace. You can export logs to S3 or BigQuery for long-term analysis or reprocessing.
05:40 Priya: Can we ingest our own logs to join on request id?
05:44 Connor: Yes if you emit the Redwood request id into your logs, you can join in your SIEM. We also support log forwarding to your Fluentd/Logstash.
05:55 Priya: Nice. Any rate limits on exporting logs?
06:00 Connor: Exports are batched - for Dedicated we can provide higher throughput exports and longer retention SLAs.
06:08 Laura: On the compliance side, are the request payloads encrypted with customer keys?
06:12 Maya: For Private and Dedicated you can use customer-managed KMS. For hosted we use our keys, but for enterprise agreements we can set up envelope encryption with your KMS.
06:25 (timestamp glitch)
06:30 Speaker 3: Uh sorry can you repeat the KMS bit?
06:33 Maya: Sure - Private/Dedicated: customer-managed KMS (HSM optional); Hosted: Redwood-managed keys by default, but envelope encryption can be arranged for enterprise. We'll send the exact architecture diagram.
06:50 Connor: Going back to debugging flows - here's a typical pattern: user reports a failure, you search traces by request id, open the trace to see which span failed, then open the request log to view the payload and tokens. If needed, you can replay with redaction and repro flags.
07:12 Ethan: How do you handle partial responses or timeouts? We see truncated responses occasionally.
07:18 Connor: Console surfaces timeout types - hard timeout vs model error vs network. For truncation we show token stream logs and whether a fallback route fired. You can configure automatic fallback to a smaller model or a cached response.
07:32 Priya: Does fallback count toward billing? We have concerns about double-charging.
07:36 Maya: We have billing controls - you can set a policy that only charges for final responses, or you can tag intermediate attempts. We'll include policy examples.
07:50 (15-minute mark in transcript condensed to highlight two longer demos)
22:10 Connor: Here's a concrete debugging example. We filtered p99 spikes to one route, saw model inference jump due to KV cache warm misses after a deploy. Console shows the deploy time and the cache miss rate spiking, which lined up with your canary rollout.
22:30 Priya: That's exactly what we needed. Can you surface cache hit rate per model variant?
22:36 Connor: Yes - metrics include cache hit/miss by model variant and route. You can also create dashboard panels for it.
22:46 Ethan: We run variable-length chats - are there tools to see sequence-length distributions?
22:50 Connor: Yes sequence-length histograms and token-per-request distributions are available in Metrics and you can cross-filter to traces.
23:05 (minor transcription error)
23:10 Connor: Sometimes the Console transcription will pick up "Redwood optimize" as "red wood optimize" in the text but that doesn't affect the underlying logs.
23:20 Priya: (laughs) Noted.
23:25 Laura: From a security reviewer perspective, we might need SAML SSO and RBAC controls.
23:32 Maya: We support SAML SSO, granular RBAC, and per-route encryption keys in Dedicated/Private. We'll include SSO docs and example RBAC roles.
23:45 Priya: One more question on latency budgets - can we set SLO-based alerts tied to customer tiers?
23:52 Connor: Yes you can create SLOs per route or per tenant and then have automatic escalation rules.
24:00 Maya: Quick recap before Q&A - we covered trace correlation, error analysis, request logs, replays, exports, and security. Next steps are to send the security pack, provision a trial account, and run a benchmark. Anything else?
24:15 Ethan: Could you also share the scripts for the benchmark and recommended traffic profile?
24:20 Connor: Yep will add to action items.
24:28 (Q&A starts - shorter back-and-forth)
29:02 Priya: Curious about non-prod instrumentation - can we use the same tracing in staging?
29:08 Connor: Absolutely, staging instruments exactly the same and you can point it to a non-prod workspace.
29:15 Priya: Great.
29:22 Laura: Minor: how are deleted logs handled? We may need deletion for GDPR requests.
29:28 Maya: We have deletion APIs and retention policies; for Hosted we'll explain the deletion SLA in the security doc. For Private you control retention.
29:40 (final 15 minutes wrap-up and scheduling)
40:05 Maya: Ok final recap and owners - I'll send the security pack and SOC2 artifacts, Connor will send benchmark plan and scripts, Priya will share sample logs. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff for next week if that works.
40:20 Priya: That works. Thanks everyone.
40:25 Ethan: Thanks.
40:30 (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional speaker mislabels and transcription artifacts. Several references to "KV cache" as "K V cash" and similar were left intact to reflect realistic transcription errors.
